stem: A 5-week-old boy is being evaluated for a weeklong history of rapid breathing and tiring during feeding.  The infant was born at home after an uneventful pregnancy.  The mother declined all prenatal testing and ultrasound evaluations.  Temperature is 36.7 C (98.1 F), blood pressure is 76/38 mm Hg, pulse is 124/min, and respirations are 66/min.  The patient's cardiovascular examination is notable for a hyperdynamic precordium and a 3/6 holosystolic murmur in the apex that radiates to the left axilla.  An echocardiogram shows defects in the interventricular septum and the lower part of the interatrial septum.  This patient's condition is most likely associated with which of the following genetic conditions?​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌
explanation:
This patient's echocardiogram findings are suggestive of an endocardial cushion defect (ie, atrioventricular canal defect), which is strongly associated with Down syndrome, an autosomal trisomy.  Failure of endocardial cushion fusion results in an ostium primum atrial septal defect (ASD); a ventricular septal defect (VSD); and (with complete failure of fusion) a single atrioventricular valve.

These abnormalities result in left-to-right shunting and atrioventricular valve regurgitation, leading to excessive pulmonary blood flow, biventricular volume overload, and symptoms of heart failure (eg, tachypnea, poor feeding) within the first year of life.  Auscultatory findings of atrioventricular valve regurgitation (holosystolic, best heard at the apex) and increased pulmonic valve blood flow (systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border) are often present.

Atrioventricular canal defects do not typically cause cyanosis unless they are left unrepaired for a prolonged period and Eisenmenger syndrome develops.

(Choice A)  DiGeorge syndrome (22q11.2 deletion) is characterized by thymic aplasia (T cell deficiency) and hypoparathyroidism (hypocalcemia).  It is associated with isolated septal defects (ASD or VSD but usually not endocardial cushion defects) and the cyanotic congenital heart defects tetralogy of Fallot and truncus arteriosus.  Tetralogy of Fallot typically does not have an ASD, and truncus arteriosus classically causes an ejection-type systolic murmur (not holosystolic).

(Choice C)  Marfan syndrome (fibrillin-1 mutation) is associated with cystic medial necrosis of the aorta, which may result in dissecting aortic aneurysms and aortic valve regurgitation.  Mitral valve prolapse is also common but septal defects are not.

(Choice D)  Mutations in frataxin, a mitochondrial protein important in iron homeostasis and respiratory function, cause Friedreich ataxia.  It is characterized by spinocerebellar degeneration and is associated with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but not septal defects.

(Choice E)  Mutations in tuberin and hamartin are seen in tuberous sclerosis.  These patients may develop cardiac rhabdomyomas in the ventricular walls and atrioventricular valves, cutaneous angiofibromas (adenoma sebaceum), CNS hamartomas, and renal cysts.  However, septal defects are not typical.

(Choice F)  A missing sex chromosome (monosomy) is seen in Turner syndrome (45,X), which is associated with bicuspid aortic valve (most common cardiac lesion) and coarctation of the aorta.

Educational objective:Atrioventricular canal defects are caused by impaired endocardial cushion fusion and are the most common congenital heart defect associated with Down syndrome.  They frequently present with a combined ostium primum atrial septal defect, a ventricular septal defect, and a single common atrioventricular valve.​‌​‌​‌​‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌‌​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌‌​​‌‌‌​‌​​​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌‌‌​​​​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌​​​‌​‌‌​‌​​​​​‌‌​‌​‌‌‌​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌​​‌​​‌​​​​‌‌​​​‌​​​‌​​​​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌​​‌‌​​‌​‌‌‌​​‌‌​‌​​​‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​‌​​‌​​‌‌‌​​‌​‌​​​​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌​​​‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​‌‌‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌​‌‌‌​‌‌‌‌​​​‌‌‌‌‌​‌​​‌‌‌‌
